thread:
kevin: Quick follow-up from the arch sync — proposal for adaptive sampling + gated promotion to reduce bench costs and surface stateful regressions earlier. Thoughts?

marta: Love the idea. Can you spell out the adaptive sampling rules? We need something deterministic enough to reproduce.

kevin: High level: 3-tier probe: smoke (inline), delta-check (short async that compares to last-promoted baseline), and full-golden. Delta-check uses adaptive sampling: start with 100 sequences, score each seq for "surprise" vs baseline (token divergence + emebedding drift), then continue sampling until uncertainty falls below threshold or budget exhausted.

lee: How do we compute "uncertainty"? Do we use standard error on divergence rate?

kevin: Yes — treat each sequence as Bernoulli (match/mismatch) and compute a running confidence interval for mismatch rate. Stop when CI width < epsilon or we've hit max_samples. Also track a running weighted divergence score (harmonic weighting to emphasize rare but high-severity mismatches).

priya: Important: delta-check must emulate runtime warmup exactly. Add a handshake flag simulate_prefix with values none|short|runtime. If runtime, prober must replay real prefix lengths and timing jitter.

marta: What about backpressure? If everyone triggers full-golden because delta flagged, bench-fleet gets overloaded. We need queuing & rate limits and a promotion policy.

kevin: Agreed. Proposal: promotion_policy is part of model registration: immediate|delayed|manual. For immediate, delta-check auto-triggers a full-golden if divergence > threshold but rate-limited per-team (tokens/day or bench_slots/day). For delayed, put in a priority queue and require an engineer ack to run full-golden. Manual always requires owner action.

lee: Good. Also suggest a cumulative golden score for each model that decays over time (exponential decay). Use that score to suppress repeated full runs for stable models; only trigger full when score drops below threshold.

priya: Operational safety: full-golden runs must be signed & auditable. Add artifact metadata: harness_version, golden_fingerprint, bench_job_id, signed_by. That helps investigate when a golden set changes.

kevin: We'll also add artifact TTLs: smoke artifacts 3d, delta-check 14d, full-golden 60d. Bench infra will enforce and garbage collect.

marta: Sampling bias: make sure adaptive sampler still includes deterministic strata for tokenization and code samples to catch tokenizer regressions. Maybe reserve 10% of quota for fixed strata.

lee: For triage UX, delta-check should return an HMAC-linked short report: top 5 mismatched sequences, divergence histogram, and a minimal repro CLI command including seed. Example:

```
rwi prober reproduce --job 12345 --seed 987 --lane delta
```

priya: Retry policy: smoke 1 retry on infra, delta-check 0 retries to preserve signal, full-golden 0 retries except on infra (no semantic retries). Also adapters should bubble transient infra codes separately from model failure codes.

orch-bot: scheduled: delta-check rwi-experimental-2 (max 500 seq, budget $15) 1m ETA; artifact will be posted to /bench/artifacts/1815004350.

kevin: One more: metric to surface: "cumulative_regression_pressure" = weighted sum of recent delta divergences normalized by sample size. Use that in dashboards to decide when to throttle promotions.

marta: And add a per-model bench_budget_usd in registration metadata so finance can auto-alert when teams exceed expected spend. Also tag promotion_policy on the model so repo-level defaults can be enforced.

lee: Implementation steps: (1) handshake schema with simulate_prefix & promotion_policy, (2) adaptive sampler + delta-check job type, (3) promotion engine with rate-limits & decay scoring, (4) CLI + triage report format, (5) docs + RFC. I'll volunteer to prototype the sampler.

priya: I'll draft the schema PR and include artifact signing fields. Kevin, can you draft the RFC with sample configs and threshold recommendations?

kevin: Will do today. If no objections I'll open the RFC and tag bench/orch/infra/finance. :+1:
